---
title: Scanners
llms-description: "How Steward scans transcripts for scoring integrity problems: the built-in scanner, choosing a scan model, adding your own, and what a finding asks of you."
---

## Overview

A sample can run, score cleanly, and still be untrustworthy: the model read the grader, refused the task while producing something that looks like an answer, or retrieved remote data from inside a sandbox that should have had no route to the internet.

Scanners review transcripts for these problems. Under Steward they run as the samples they review complete, so the transcripts are already scanned by the time the run finishes.

Steward runs a scoring integrity scanner over every sample of every run. It requires no configuration.

## Scan Model

By default a scanner reviews with the model already under evaluation, so an unconfigured run still scans. To use a different model, set `scan_model` in `_steward.yaml` or `STEWARD_SCAN_MODEL` in your `.env`:

```{.yaml filename="_steward.yaml"}
scan_model: anthropic/claude-opus-5
```

A scanner that names its own model in the definition keeps it.

## Adding Scanners

Your definition is the normal place to say what scans your eval set:

```{.python filename="evalset.py"}
eval_set(
    tasks=[cais_swebenchpro(), datacurve_deep_swe()],
    model=["openai/gpt-5.6-sol", "anthropic/claude-opus-5"],
    scanner=[my_scanner()],
)
```

## Findings

A flagged sample becomes an anomaly and is decided the same way an error is, as described in [Error Handling](errors.qmd). Samples flagged the same way in the same task are one class and one decision, and every disposition is available, including excluding or zeroing a score you establish is wrong.

Nothing is put to you while the task is still running. When it lands, your agent investigates every finding the task has and brings them to you together, one row per class with a proposed disposition, and your answers are recorded row by row. A finding ruled on one task is shown as precedent when another task lands with the same one, and the task's finished notification goes out with the proposals.

Most findings change no score, and those are still put to you: a model that refused, or probed a grader it never reached, earned nothing, and its row proposes keeping the score as recorded so the report carries the finding. Dismissing is for a flag the transcript does not bear out. A run cannot be signed off while a finding has no ruling either way, and at signoff Steward tells you how many were dismissed and your agent is asked to name them.
